response: Chembur (M/W) billed INR 4689823 against a budget of INR 4400000 this monsoon, or 106.6 percent, across 87 jobs. Of these, 27.6 percent were reopened within 30 days and 56.3 percent met their deadline. The city had 18 days of heavy or worse rain, and Chembur is a low lying ward (index 0.6) where flooding is common, so some repeat damage is expected. Still, INR 1275227 was billed on DLP roads. DLP means a road is still under the original contractor's warranty, so repairs should cost the city nothing. This spending needs review. Also, 4 jobs exceeded the rate card by more than the 30 percent tolerance and should be checked. Konkan Roadcon Pvt Ltd (synthetic) was the top contractor by spend. Example work orders are WO25-00003 and WO25-01151. Ask the ward office whether WO25-00003 was on a DLP road and, if so, why the city paid.
